components.label: header
components.name: Header
components.description:
What the Component Does
Provides the application’s top header, bringing together platform branding, a menu icon, and the user’s avatar-menu access point. Its primary use is to maintain a consistent application shell while exposing relevant top-level controls. The Taxonomy presentation additionally includes a search area.

This is the application header, not a content-card header. Platform navigation remains in the left-hand menu, and account/help/preferences content is supplied through the avatar menu.

Variants and Controls
• Version=Default: the default presentation, containing the Business@Slalom branding, menu icon, and nested avatar menu.
• Version=Taxonomy: contains the branding and menu icon, plus a Function Group with a Search presentation and nested avatar menu.
• Version is the only exposed Header property. There are no header-level text properties, visibility switches, content slots, or responsive/open-state variants.
• Both nested avatar menus use status=Default in the samples. Configure their identity information, content slots, and opened/closed presentation through the avatar menu component, following its documented application-specific guidance.
• The menu element is an icon instance, not the contextual action-menu component. Its presence does not establish a navigation-expansion interaction.
• Search in Version=Taxonomy is a frame containing a search icon and “Search” text. It is a visual presentation, not a functioning text input or an exposed Header search

components.label: container
components.name: container
components.description:
What the Component Does?

Provides the base layout surface for page content sections. Use containers to group related section content consistently and follow the applicable product’s layout rules for placement, arrangement, and content composition.


Standard content inside containers must maintain 32 px padding for consistency. The minimum container width is 460 px, corresponding to the minimum breakpoint. 

Do not reduce the container below this width or reduce standard content padding to fit a narrower layout.

Variants and Controls
• type=general container: the default variant for content sections without an embedded table. The container has 32 px padding on all four sides and a minimum width of 460 px.

• type=table container: the table-specific version referred to in product guidance as Type B. Select this variant whenever a container includes a table.

• header: a content slot available in both variants. In general container, it is the available slot for section content; in table container, use it for the heading, controls, or other content above the table.

• Table slot: available only in table container. Insert the table here, not inside the padded header area. This slot has 0 px padding on all sides.

• Both variants use a vertical layout and have a 460 px minimum width. The sample width is 1400 px, not a required usage width.

• Current table-container spacing: the outer frame has 32 px top, 0 px side, and 16 px bottom padding; its header supplies 32 px left/right

components.label: card
components.name: card
components.description:
What the Component Does?

Groups related content and its supporting actions into a distinct surface.

Its primary use is to present one coherent topic, record, summary, or task with a header, body, and optional call-to-action area, making the content easy to scan within a larger page.

Variants and Controls

• Type=elevated: a card presentation for visually separating content from its surrounding surface. Supports status=Default, hover, and banner.
• Type=tonal: an alternate surface treatment for grouped content. Supports status=Default only.

• type=small: a compact card presentation. Supports status=Default and hover.

• status=Default: resting presentation.

• status=hover: pointer-over presentation; it does not establish that the entire card is clickable.

• status=banner: a distinct header/banner presentation, not an interaction state. Available only for elevated cards.

• primary color: a variant axis with values true and false, available for each supported type/status combination. Use the matching color treatment for the surrounding design; this is a variant selector, not a Boolean visibility control.

• The set contains 12 variants, not every possible combination of its axes. Current Figma default: type=elevated, status=Default, primary color=true.

Content controls:

• header slot: supplies the card header. Default and hover samples contain a nested card header; banner samples use a different header composition.

• content Slot: supplies the main body; empty in the s

components.label: cardHeader
components.name: card header
components.description:
What the Component Does
Provides the title area for the main card component, with optional leading/trailing icons and a subtitle where supported. Its primary use is to identify the card’s content and provide relevant header affordances while keeping the card’s heading consistent.

This is a supporting component for the main card’s header slot. Usage is restricted to the main card component; it is not a standalone page, container, dialog, or specialized-card header.

Variants and Controls
• Property 1=center-header: the default centered-header presentation, with title and optional icons in a horizontal row.
• Property 1=left-header: a left-aligned header presentation with an optional subtitle beneath the title row.
• Title sm: controls visibility of the small-title presentation; default is false.
• title lg: controls visibility of the large-title presentation; default is true. Use one title presentation at a time rather than showing both.
• right icon: controls the trailing icon; default is true.
• left icon: controls the leading icon; default is false.
• has subtitle: controls the subtitle in the left-header presentation; default is false. The center-header variant contains no subtitle presentation.
• Replace “Card Title” and “Card subtitle” with meaningful content through the relevant text layers. Title and subtitle text are not exposed as component-level text properties.
• The default icon artwork is sample content, not a prescribed action. Choose icons that accurately repr

components.label: button
components.name: button
components.description:
What the Component Does?
Provides a reusable button for initiating a user action, with labeled and icon-only presentations. Variants control visual emphasis, size, and interaction-state appearance.

Properties:
• size: lg, md, sm.
• variant: contained_button, outlined, text, Plain, neutral_outlined, icon, icon contained.
• status: enabled, disabled, hover, pressed. The sync status displays a loading indicator and is available only for contained_button and neutral_outlined, in all three sizes.

• Text sets the label (default: “Button”). icon-left and icon right control optional leading and trailing icons on labeled variants; both default to true. All button labels are Title Case by default (title case=true; uppercase=false).
• Default usage: size=md, variant=contained_button, status=enabled.
• These variants represent visual states; application behavior must be implemented separately.

Use Cases

Recommended usage:
• contained_button: a prominent primary action, such as Save or Submit.
• outlined: a secondary action that needs a visible boundary without a filled background.
• neutral_outlined: a secondary or supporting action with neutral visual emphasis, such as Cancel.
• text: a low-emphasis action alongside more prominent buttons.
• Plain: a minimal, neutral action within supporting content.
• icon: a compact icon-only action in a toolbar or repeated row.
• icon contained: an icon-only action that needs stronger filled emphasis.
• md: the default button size. Use for action

components.label: semanticButton
components.name: semantic Buttons
components.description:
What the Component Does

Provides action buttons with negative or positive semantic emphasis. Use negative for destructive actions such as Remove or Delete; use positive when an action needs positive semantic emphasis.

As with the main buttons, contained_button provides the highest visual hierarchy and is used only when the action is standalone. Outlined provides lower emphasis for actions within tables, lists, and action groups.

Available variants and controls:
• semantic: negative, positive.
• variant: contained_button, outlined.
• Size: lg, md, sm.
• status: default (available action), hover (pointer-over feedback), pressed (active press feedback), disable (unavailable action).
• All 48 combinations of semantic, variant, Size, and status are available.
• label controls the button text (default: “Button”). icon left and icon right control optional icons; both default to true.
• Labels are Title Case by default (Title Case=true; Upper Case=false), consistent with the main buttons.
• Status variants represent visual states; application behavior must be implemented separately.

Use Cases and Exceptions

Hierarchy and size guidance:
• Standalone actions: use contained_button only when the action stands alone and requires the highest emphasis.
• lg: use only when the button is beside a field, consistent with the main buttons.

Negative actions:
• Highlighted Remove or Delete action in a section: use negative + contained_button + md when the action is standalone and needs promi

components.label: textField
components.name: input/textField
components.default: state=input, has value=textField, Label style=label on
components.description:
What the Component Does
Collects a single line of user-entered text with a visible label and optional supporting feedback. Use type=label on when the label sits above the field and type=label in when the label is integrated into the field. Choose has value=true for populated fields and false for empty fields where available. Set state to enabled, hover, focused, error, or disabled to match the current interaction and validation state.


Use Cases
• Forms that collect names, titles, dates, search terms, or other short values.
• Showing hover and focus feedback during entry.
• Communicating validation problems with the error state and supporting message.
• Displaying read-only unavailable controls with the disabled state.


Exceptions

components.label: textArea
components.name: text area
components.description:
What the Component Does
Collects multi-line text with configurable labeling, guidance, validation, and resize affordances. Use type=label on when the label sits above the field and label in when it is integrated into the field. Set has value to true or false where available, and choose status=enable, hover, focused, error, or disable to match the current interaction state. Configure the label, content, assistive, and error text; use is required, user guidance, assistive text, error text, and has label to control supporting information. Use drag horizontal and drag corner to show the appropriate resize affordances.


Use Cases
• Collecting descriptions, comments, notes, feedback, or other longer responses.
• Showing assistive guidance, required status, and validation errors.
• Providing hover, focus, and disabled feedback during form entry.
• Allowing users to resize the field when the experience supports it.


Exceptions

components.label: singleSelect
components.name: single-select
components.description:
What the Component Does
Lets users choose one option from a predefined list. Use type=label on when the label sits above the field and label-in when it is integrated into the field. Set has value to true or false where available, and choose status=enable, hover, focused, error, or disable to match the current state. Configure the label, dropdown, assistive, and error text; use show text or show chip group for the selected-value treatment. Control required status, user guidance, and the optional left icon with the available properties.


Use Cases
• Forms and settings where exactly one predefined option can be selected.
• Filters, categories, statuses, locations, or assignment choices.
• Showing selected values as text or an approved chip treatment.
• Providing guidance, validation feedback, and disabled states.


Exceptions

components.label: autocomplete
components.name: autocomplete
components.description:
What the Component Does
Lets users type to find and select a value from a suggested set of options. Use type=label on when the label sits above the field and label in when it is integrated into the field. Set has value to true or false where available, and choose status=enable, hover, focus, filled, error, or disable to match the current state. Configure labels, input, assistive, and error text; use text response or chips for the selected-value treatment. Control required status, guidance, icons, dropdown arrow, and clear action with the available properties.


Use Cases
• Searching and selecting from long option lists such as people, projects, locations, or categories.
• Supporting single-value text selections or chip-based selections.
• Showing focus, filled, error, and disabled form states.
• Providing guidance, validation, clearing, and dropdown affordances.


Exceptions

components.label: datePicker
components.name: date picker
components.description:
What the Component Does
Provides a calendar control for choosing a day, month, or year. Use the sections property to display the day selector, month selector, or year selector. Use status to show default, hover, selected, or current selected states where available. Use rounded border to switch between square and rounded containers, and update the mm/yy label text property for the displayed month or year label.

Use Cases
• Selecting a date in forms, filters, scheduling, booking, or reporting flows.
• Moving between day, month, and year selection views.
• Showing hover feedback, a chosen value, or the currently selected date.
• Matching layouts that require either rounded or square picker containers.

Exceptions

components.label: radio
components.name: radio button
components.description:
What the Component Does
Lets users choose one option from a mutually exclusive group. Use status=default for an unselected option and selected for the chosen option. Set Size to sm, md, or lg to match the density and hierarchy of the surrounding interface. Keep only one radio button selected within each group.


Use Cases
• Forms and settings where users must choose exactly one option.
• Selecting a plan, preference, method, or other mutually exclusive value.
• Adapting the control size for compact, standard, or spacious layouts.


Exceptions

components.label: switch
components.name: Switch Toggle
components.description:
What the Component Does
Controls a binary setting that can be turned on or off. Set Toggle Status to Off or On to reflect the current value, and set State to Enabled when the control is available or Disabled when it cannot be changed. Keep the visual status synchronized with the underlying setting.


Use Cases
• Enabling or disabling settings, preferences, features, or visibility.
• Providing an immediate binary choice without a separate submit action.
• Showing an existing on or off value that is temporarily unavailable with the disabled state.


Exceptions

components.label: listItem
components.name: list item
components.description:
What the Component Does?

Represents one item in a list, combining a primary label with optional icons, supporting descriptions, a toggle, and status information. Its primary use is to present related entries in a consistent, scannable row; a row can indicate navigation, expose a setting, or communicate an item’s status according to the surrounding context.

Variants and Controls

-Status

• Default: the default row presentation.

• secondary: an alternate visual presentation. Its name does not define selected, hover, or disabled behavior; use according to the surrounding design’s hierarchy.

• errored: error-emphasis presentation with optional information icon and status chip.

• queued: queued-status presentation with optional information icon and status chip. Do not treat a queued item as disabled solely because of its visual styling.

Content and visibility controls:

• label: primary text; default is “Section Label”.

• has icon: shows the leading icon; default is true. Instance swaps the leading icon component.

• directional: shows the trailing navigation indicator; default is true.

• bottom description and right description: show supporting text below the label or on the right; both default to false. Replace their sample text when shown.

• has toggle: shows the switch; default is false.

• right icon: shows an additional trailing icon; default is false.

• has chip and info icon: show status elements in errored and queued variants; both default to true.

• These con

components.label: listSection
components.name: list-section
components.description:
What the Component Does?
Groups related list items into a single vertical section with an optional section title and bottom divider. Its primary use is to organize a menu or modal’s entries into clear, scannable groups while keeping row presentation consistent.

Variants and Controls
• Type=menu lists: the default section presentation. The sample content contains three list item instances with leading icons and trailing directional indicators, suitable for grouped navigation entries.

 type=modal lists: a section presentation for modal content. The sample rows use the secondary list item presentation with leading grip-style icons, right-side metadata, and trailing delete icons; directional indicators are hidden.
• list container slot: supplies the section’s list content. Both variants contain three sample rows; this is sample content, not a documented three-item limit.
• has title: shows or hides the header; default is true. Replace “Section title” with a descriptive group title. Title text is not exposed as a section-level text property.
• divider: shows or hides the bottom divider; default is true.

• Row labels, icons, metadata, toggles, and status presentations belong to the nested list items, not the section-level controls. Configure those through the list content.
• The section uses a vertical layout: header, list content, then divider.

• The variants define visual presentation only. Navigation, deletion, reordering, selection, and scrolling must be configured separate

components.label: avatar
components.name: v-avatar
components.description:
What the Component Does
Displays a user's identity as either initials or an image. Choose the image version property to switch between the initials and image variants. Select xs, s, m, lg, or xl with the size property, and update the user initials text property when using initials.


Use Cases
• Representing people in navigation, profiles, comments, tables, lists, and activity feeds.
• Using initials when no profile image is available.
• Selecting a size that matches the density and hierarchy of the surrounding interface.


Exceptions

components.label: modal
components.name: modal
components.description:
What the Component Does?

Presents focused information, a decision, or a task in a dialog without requiring users to leave the current product context. 
Use dialogs to ensure users understand relevant product information, respond to important warnings or urgent decisions, or enter data and perform system-related tasks.


Variants and Controls

• type=alert: informs users about important warnings or decisions requiring urgent attention. Keep the message and response focused on the immediate issue.

• type=data: supports information and knowledge introduction, including data definitions, terminology, tutorials, and guidance; also supports relevant data entry and task workflows that need more content space.

• type=announcement: highlights relevant launches or information users need to know, such as policies or new features. Uses a distinct banner-style header.

• rounded corner: a variant axis with values true and false. The set contains both treatments, but permitted usage is restricted to rounded corner=true for alert, data, and announcement. 

Use a 24 px corner radius (radius-xl) and 24 px dialog content padding on all sides (pa-6). 

The 24 px radius is corner rounding, not border stroke thickness. Do not use rounded corner=false or override these radius and padding values.


• Current Figma default: type=alert, rounded corner=true.

• content slot: supplies the dialog body. Insert the relevant information, warning, form, or task content; sample bodies are empty.

• CTA Se

components.label: contentSlot
components.name: content-slot
components.description:
What the Component Does
Provides the descriptive body text for the main card component. Its primary use is to explain the card’s subject or supply supporting information between the header and any related actions, using a consistent centered or left-aligned presentation.

Usage is restricted to the main card component’s content area. Despite its name, content-slot is a component set containing text, not an exposed content slot for arbitrary inserted content.

Variants and Controls
• type=content-centered: the default variant; the visible body text is center-aligned.
• type=content-left: the visible body text is left-aligned. Select based on the parent card’s content hierarchy and product rules.
• type is the only exposed property. There are no top-level text, visibility, instance-swap, or content-slot controls.
• Both variants contain a visible text layer named Subtitle with placeholder body copy. Replace its content through the relevant text layer; the layer name does not make it the card header’s subtitle.
• The visible body text uses truncation in a fixed sample area. Longer copy may be clipped or truncated; do not assume automatic height growth or an included Read More action.
• Each variant also contains a hidden Description-left frame. It is not a separate exposed control and is not the visible text source; do not populate hidden content instead of the active text.
• The variant names describe text alignment. The visible frame is named Description-Centered in both varia

components.label: statusAlertBar
components.name: Status Alert Bar
components.description:
What the Component Does
Displays a full-width status message using warning, error, or informative styling. Choose Type based on message severity. Choose Function=Closeable for dismissible alerts, Info for an informational affordance, Button Action for a labeled button, or Hyperlink Action for an inline link where that combination is available. Update the corresponding message and CTA text properties, use Show Icon to control the leading status icon, and use Show Modal Pop-up when the configured action should expose a modal.


Use Cases
• Warning users about conditions that may require attention.
• Reporting errors that block or interrupt a task.
• Sharing neutral system or workflow information.
• Providing dismissal, more information, a button action, or a hyperlink action when supported by the selected type.


Exceptions

components.label: toast
components.name: Toast Notifications
components.description:
What the Component Does
Displays a brief status notification without interrupting the current workflow. Choose State=Information for neutral updates, Error Toast for failed actions or problems, and Success for completed actions. Update the corresponding message text property, use Has CTA to show or hide the action, and use Show Icon to control the leading status icon.


Use Cases
• Confirming that an action completed successfully.
• Brief message display that typically will disappear after a few seconds. The time parameter can be adjusted as needed.
• Reporting an error after a user or system action.
• Sharing short, non-blocking informational updates.
• Including a relevant follow-up action when the user can immediately respond.


Exceptions

components.label: step
components.name: step
components.default: horizontal label=true, horizontal line=true, status=current step
components.description:
What the Component Does
Combines a step indicator, label, and optional connector into one stepper item. Update the step description text property for the label. Use status=current step for the active step, completed for a finished step, and Next Step for an upcoming step. Set horizontal label to control the label orientation, horizontal line to control the connector orientation, and connector line to show or hide the connector—typically hiding it on the final step.


Use Cases
• Building horizontal or vertical steppers for forms, onboarding, setup, and checkout.
• Showing completed, active, and upcoming steps with descriptive labels.
• Mixing label and connector orientations to fit the available layout.
• Removing the connector from the final item in a sequence.


Exceptions

components.label: stepCounter
components.name: step counter
components.description:
What the Component Does
Displays the position and progress of one step in a multi-step flow. Update the step text property with the step number. Use status=completed for a finished step, current for the active step, and next for an upcoming step.


Use Cases
• Multi-step forms, setup flows, onboarding, and checkout processes.
• Showing which steps are complete, active, or still ahead.
• Combining multiple instances into a progress indicator or stepper.


Exceptions

components.label: accordionRow
components.name: Accordion Row
components.description:
What the Component Does

Organizes related information into a row with a visible header and an expandable content area.

Its primary use is progressive disclosure: keep the section title visible while showing detailed content only when the row is expanded, reducing clutter without leaving the current view.

Variants:
• Type=custom: a preconfigured detail layout with status information, a progress ring, labeled detail rows, and a comments/notes group this is the version only for engagement summary.

• Type=general: a flexible layout with a header slot and content slot for context-specific content. The content slot is empty by default and must be populated for a meaningful expanded view.

• status=Collapsed: header visible; content hidden.

• status=Collapsed Hover: collapsed presentation with pointer-over feedback.

• status=Expanded: header and content visible.

• status=Expanded Hover: expanded presentation with pointer-over feedback.

• Both types support all four statuses, for eight variants. The current Figma default is Type=custom, status=Collapsed.

Use Case and exceptions
The custom version is only for Engagement Summary section. For all the other applications the recommended version is the general version.

components.label: emptyState
components.name: empty State
components.description:
What the Component Does
Communicates that a page, section, or collection has no content yet by pairing an illustration with a title, supporting message, and optional call to action. Use Type=horizontal for a compact side-by-side arrangement and Type=vertical for a centered stacked arrangement. Use has CTA to show or hide the action.


Use Cases
• First-use experiences where content has not been created yet.
• Search, filter, or data views that return no results.
• Empty sections that need explanation and a clear next step.
• Horizontal layouts in shorter or wider spaces, and vertical layouts in larger centered spaces.


Exceptions
There some scenarios where we can remove or reduce the size of the illustration

components.label: combobox
components.name: combobox
components.description:
What the Component Does
Combines text entry with option selection and optional adjacent actions. Set Status to enable, hover, focused, filled, error, or disable to match the current interaction and validation state. Configure the label, description, and assistive content; use mandatory, user guidance, has label, assistive text, error text, and has icon to control supporting information. Use button1 and button2 to show or hide the available companion actions.


Use Cases
• Forms where users can type a value or choose from suggested options.
• Selecting known items while still supporting direct text entry.
• Showing one or two related actions beside the field.
• Providing required status, guidance, validation feedback, and disabled states.


Exceptions
